Hello hello TahskaAjuha! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

Speaking of which, let's click it, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

Hello SCP Wiki Forums!

I've recently taken an interest in this place when SCP animation videos started showing up in my YouTube feed, particularly ones from the spin-off channel of the Infographics channel. Technically, I've known about the existence of SCPs since around 2014, courtesy of Tumblr, but I've never really thought of actually trying to write stories set in the SCP Universe until now.

Hello! After years of being too lazy to join, I finally made an account. Believe it or not, I've actually been a fan of the SCP Wiki since elementary school, probably around fourth grade? I was introduced to it by my sister, who just really liked giving me nightmares. I was instantly hooked though; I have vivid memories of browsing random articles on the school laptops when I probably wasn't supposed to. I've been in love with horror and weird fiction since, and it's honestly a huge influence on who I am today.

Though I've been a fan for awhile now, I recently rediscovered how much I love this website. For the past few days I've been doing NOTHING but reading SCP articles, drawing fanart, writing fanfic, and resisting the urge to annoy my friends by rambling about it. Now I'm really interested in writing my own SCP, and though I'm super nervous, I'm having a ton of fun coming up with ideas.

I'm constantly amazed by the sheer amount of creativity and talent in this community, and I'm thrilled to eventually contribute to it myself. =)

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
How do you do. I'm Piecemaker and I am honored to at last find myself in the Foundation.

I've been reading through various documentation for years with many favorites to speak of, and have recently decided it might be time for me to write one of my own. I'm gathered numerous experiences over the years through games, books, movies and I've always had a thing for creepy or unsettling things, which is why I often recommend SCP to my colleagues and friends.

That being said, I wish for my first document to be on a humanoid SCP. I have a rather specific concept in mind that I've been going over in my head for weeks. Now, I know, it's not recommended to start with a humanoid. How do I know? Because I've read through every guide I could get my hands on, from "So you wanna write a humanoid" to "Things what do a thing", as well as going through some 50 crits in the Ideas critique forum to see common pitfalls. I am nevertheless terrified of falling into an X-man syndrome or another common mistake, as the concept is rather close to me. Either way, I intend to give it my very best effort. See you in the Crit Forum.
